analysis: The item-bias attempt failed the frozen host’s post-training correctness check: forward scores must equal embedding dot products, but learned item intercepts violate that requirement. Zero initialization hides the mismatch initially; training makes it observable. Reported validation HR@10 peaked at 0.630 at epochs 20 and 40, below the 0.635 baseline. The run crashed after epoch 40, so no completed 60-epoch result is available. Discard this candidate; future changes must preserve pure dot-product scoring under the unchanged host.
code_summary: Position-free NextItNet with 64-dimensional tied item embeddings, eight independent causal convolution blocks, and dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8]. Each block gates dilated and depthwise local convolution branches, then applies GELU, dropout, a second dilated convolution, and a learned per-channel residual scale. Layer normalization and padding masks preserve sequence behavior; candidate scoring selects the last nonpadding state. This attempt added zero-initialized scalar item biases to training and candidate scores. Hyperparameters remained MAXLEN=128, KERNEL_SIZE=3, DROPOUT_RATE=0.2, LR=0.001, WEIGHT_DECAY=0.0, and BATCH_SIZE=128.
